utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, this is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness AA. Witness AA, did there come a time in -- during your detention at the MUP station that a person was brought in your cell by the name of Ibrahim Badzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And can you tell us about this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they brought him to the cell, he had a swelling under his eye. I don't know whether it was the right or the left one. And when we asked him what had happened, he said that Stela's men had come, thrown him out of the house and punched him at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, I look at the transcript and the last name of this person did not come out correctly. Could you spell his last name, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: B-A-D-Z-A-K.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now for how many weeks?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please come closer to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I think you'll have to move -- yeah. How many weeks were you detained in the MUP station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, you testified about the fact -- about the first evening that Romeo had come into your cell. Was there another occasion that soldiers came to the cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: When was this, and what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was over a weekend, a Saturday or Sunday, I don't know exactly, when none of the permanent staff were there. We heard first somebody descending the stairs, then the door of the cell beside me opened, we heard the prisoner being taken out, and after that, in the room where we were having our -- from the room where we were having our meals, we could hear beating, we could hear blows. And when they brought him back to the cell, then they opened my cell, and they immediately pulled me out of it, and I found myself facing four or five soldiers. They started beating me straight away. I tried to shield myself and reached a cupboard, so I pressed myself against it and with my hands, and foot, I tried to shield myself so that they wouldn't hurt me too much, but they were beating me around the kidneys and on that leg that I was standing on, and when they got too tired of that, then they threw me in the middle of the room and ordered me to do push-ups, and one of the soldiers who was rather short --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Can I just stop you there? You said these were soldiers. Do you recognise -- do you know from which unit these soldiers were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those soldiers came from the Convicts' Battalion Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they had a patch on their left arm, which was affixed with a needle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And what did this patch say? What was on the patch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The patch said, Convicts' Battalion, in a semi-circle, under it Siroki Brijeg, or the other way around, Siroki Brijeg first and the Convicts' Battalion below it, and in the centre, there was an emblem or something, I know it was black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, before I interrupted you, you said that the soldiers -- one of the soldiers asked you to do push-ups. Who was this -- did you catch the name of that person who asked to you do push-ups and what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear the name of that person. When they made me do the push-ups, he sat down on me and wanted me to lift him too while doing the push-ups. After that, a soldier came, whom I had already mentioned earlier, whose name I do not know, who had beaten Meho Zelic and myself, and he then said that I had entered Branko Kvesic's room and stolen something from it, stolen some papers from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sorry. Can I just -- you said, "whom I already mentioned earlier." Are you now referring to the time that you were taken to the MUP station on the day -- on the day that you were taken to the MUP station, that you were lined up before the MUP station? Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. He had a pistol in his hand and said that I was no Muslim, that Muslims were clean, and that I stank. Then he pointed his pistol at me and it fired, but all I heard was the sound of the pin. And then he went out and I stayed behind with soldiers. And then they told me later on that I had to betray somebody, that I had to tell on somebody who had been in the command with me. And I pointed at only two men, one from the left-hand cell and one from my cell. And before that --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Before we get to that, so you said -- do you remember the person who asked you to point out two men from the cell? Do you remember the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember his name. I apologise. I forgot to say: When that man with the pistol came, he asked me about a tall, fair guy, I mean tall, about two metres. And he asked me if I knew him, and I said I didn't. And he then said that that was the brother of the late Croat knight. I can't remember his name now. It just escapes me right now. What is it? Cikota, Cikota's brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And was this man which you referred to as Cikota's brother, was he one of the soldiers there present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was one of the soldiers who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Was he also the man who asked you then to point out two people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He asked me to point out at two men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me to point out at two men, and if I lied, that he would tear off my balls. After that, I entered the cell to the right of me and pointed at a man, and I also had to indicate another man from the cell, and they took them with them and left me in the passage to wait. They took one of those out. I think that that guy was from Stolac or somewhere. But I mean, he was from East Herzegovina. And they only slapped him in the face and made him go back into the cell. The other man was Basic. He came from Gacko. And since he refused to tell them anything, they punched him in the nose. He started to bleed, and he was also returned to the cell. After that, they took me back into that room once again, and Cikota's brother lit a cigarette, took several smokes, told me to open my mouth and stick out my tongue, and he extinguished his cigarette on my tongue and then put the cigarette in my mouth and forced me to swallow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you indeed swallow the cigarette?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had to. And then they told me to hit the wall with my head ten times. And the first two times I just hit gently so as not to get injured, but then they told me that I had to hit it stronger. And I ten times then hit the wall with my head and had to count it all. After that they returned me to the cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You testified that you stayed for two weeks in the MUP station. Where were you taken after your detention at the MUP station? And do you recall around what date this was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date. It was about a fortnight. They told us to go to Ljubuski because they had the central prison there for the exchange of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did all the prisoners from the MUP station, were they all transported to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the prisoners that were there with me were taken to Ljubuski from the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: When you arrived at the Ljubuski prison, were there any other prisoners at the Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived at Ljubuski, there was already that group of Sovicans who had been detained before us, and there were also four men from Stolac who had been sentenced to a six-day term, and there was a group in the cell from Mostar who had been in the command of the 4th Corps, some five or six of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What did these people from Sovici, what did they tell you what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Men from Sovici said that when the attack had started against them and that they had been attacked by Tuta's units, and since they had dispersed around the village - I don't know how - that after that they called them over a loudspeaker to come down to the school and surrender and reach an agreement as to what next.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit P9.8 and 9.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, witness, can you recognise the building that you were kept in, or on this -- on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I recognise is this building, because these two tall buildings were not there when I was there, so that -- but this is that building behind it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Were you saying that the big brown building and the white building on the left of it were not there at the time you were detained at Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, was there anything else on the spot where the white building is now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, there should be a building, a U-shaped building with cells.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Is that where the prisoners were kept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If the witness now can be shown the next exhibit, 9.9?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You recognise this building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the building that I mentioned a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Okay. That's enough for these exhibits. Now, while you were at Ljubuski, Witness AA, did you meet a prisoner by the name of Rudi Jozelic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rudi Jozelic was a member of the BiH army, and during the attack on the command, he was acting -- an acting officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did Rudi told you what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that on the 10th of May, sometime around 9.00 or 10.00 in the evening, Romeo and Tahic had come to the prison, lined them up, and he was handcuffed with his hands on his back. And at that moment, Romeo took a shovel to beat him over his body, exposed body, and that he -- all his ribs cracked on that occasion, and that his -- and his nose was injured and his waistcoat was all bloody, and he also said that he had to be extended medical aid after that. And when they took off the handcuffs, his nose was also broken and he repaired it himself. He straightened it up himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, how was this man Rudi treated at the Ljubuski prison at the time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was there, Rudi was mistreated by military policeman called Petkovic. He once forced him to sing the Croatian anthem, and when Rudi was about to sing it, he started to hit him and said, "Traitors will not sing the Croatian anthem." His wife was a Muslim namely and he forced him also to pray the Muslim way. And he didn't know how. And he was then beaten again. And then he threw him on a table where we usually had our meals, and then he would jump on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, was Rudi also interrogated by people during his detention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did he tell you by whom he was interrogated and what the interrogators asked him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was interrogated by the Croatian military and what they wanted to know most was were the Serbs about to make an assault and where should it happen? And they also wanted him to join the Croat troops, because he was an instructor pilot, he knew how to fly a helicopter, for a salary, but Rudi refused to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: At the time that you were detained in Ljubuski, did the man you referred to as Cikota, did he ever visit at Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One Saturday during my stay in Ljubuski, or perhaps it was Sunday, Cikota came to Ljubuski too. On that occasion, we all had to enter the cells, and my cell was open and I saw Cikota through the door. He stood in the doorway, and when he saw me, he said, "Well, we don't seem to be feeding you particularly well. You seem to have lost some weight. You don't look too well." After that, he entered Rudi's cell, because the cells were one beside the other, so I could overhear the conversation, and he said to Rudi, "Didn't I tell you, pilot, that who flies high falls low?" And from that cell, they took Rudi out, they took Kajtaz out, Dzemo, and Alija Lizde.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What did they do to these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No sooner were they out than Dzemo was hit with a stick and he fell immediately. And Rudi and Kajtaz were forced to slap one another in the face.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you see this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't, because I was locked in my cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: But did you hear later what happened from Rudi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later, when they left, we were released from our cells. We were all in the yard, and that is when they told me what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, for how long were you detained at Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that we were kept in Ljubuski until -- for about two or three weeks. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And where were you taken after Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Ljubuski, they took us to Heliodrom, to the central prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed at the Heliodrom until the 30th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What happened on that day, on the 30th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 30th of June, since the army had liberated the northern camp, all members of the Muslim ethnicity were brought to the Heliodrom. Since there was no more room for them to place the Muslims, the Heliodrom was full, they took us from two rooms where we were detained, and transferred us to Dretelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, you say that the Muslims were brought, that people were -- Muslims were brought to the Heliodrom. Can you make an estimate of how many people were actually arrived on the 30th of June at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that exactly, but buses constantly were arriving full of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So you were then taken to Dretelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 21.8, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise what is depicted on this photograph, Witness AA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a hangar on this photograph here, and then above that there are two bunkers. This is where the former JNA kept its fuel. And here we can see these small buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, where were you kept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was kept here, in this hangar that is made of tin.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And how many people were kept in this hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were from 500 to 700 people at the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And you pointed out to the other locations. Were prisoners also kept in the other locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could you estimate how many prisoners in total were kept in Dretelj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps there were 3.000 prisoners at Dretelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness AA, could you briefly describe the conditions in Dretelj at the time that you were detained.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conditions at Dretelj were very difficult, and it was the most difficult of all the camps to be in. From the 15th of July to the 15th of August, or from the 15th of June, when the army had liberated some area around Stolac, we didn't receive water for three days and we received no food for four days. They kept us shut up. And during those four days, they would shoot fragmenting bullets in the hangar at us. And then because of that, there were about ten wounded, because the building had armoured glass, reinforced glass, and then these pieces of glass fell all over us. All of us had to lie down on the floor, because if we got up, we would be hit by a bullet. They wouldn't let us go to the bathroom, so that we had to do that in one corner of the hangar. First we would do it in jars. Then we were afraid that they would make us drink it. So then we broke a hole through the wall of the hangar, and that's where we then went to the bathroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, how long did you stay at Dretelj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed at Dretelj for 20 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And where were you taken after your detention in Dretelj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Dretelj, I was returned to the Heliodrom again, but then, when they returned me, I was in the sports -- in the gymnasium. And then after the gymnasium, I was transferred to the central prison again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: During this second time that you were detained in the Heliodrom, did you ever have to do labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Where did you have to do this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion I had to go to the trenches. They loaded us into trucks, and then first, when they were allocating the groups, my group was taken behind the Rondo. A group of Stela's boys were there. They were looking for Romeo, to wake him up so that they could take us to the trenches. And because they couldn't wake him up to take us to Santic, they got somebody else to take us. And there at Santic, we had to carry sacks in order to build these bunkers. At one point somebody asked for one prisoner, and they sent me, and they said, "Here's one from Vranica."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Can I just ask you a question? So can you indicate the location where you actually were carrying these sacks? Where was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were carrying the sacks towards the line with the army, and that's how we made it possible for them to get closer. Otherwise we also had to use the bags to block all the passages so that they couldn't shoot at them, and we did this, for example, between two buildings, and it was a distance of ten to fifteen metres. The other prisoners would bring the sacks to these buildings and I was forced to construct the bunkers out in the open.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of the street where this was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Santiceva Street. When I had made a barrier at that passage, one of the soldiers forced me to sit on those bags and to place my legs on the side of the line against the army, and then he placed his rifle on my shoulder and fired one bullet. After that, he fired two more bullets, resting his gun on my shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Who was this soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was an HVO soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And what happened after he fired his gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no response from the other side, even though while I was sitting on the sacks he was pointing to my left shoulder for them to hit me. After that, they brought us back to the Heliodrom again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: When were you released from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was released from the Heliodrom on the 19th of March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. President, I have one more issue to deal with this witness, but I'd like to do that in private session, because it will reveal probably his identity if we would do it in public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examinations? Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness AA. How are you today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: My name is Mr. Meek and I am one of the counsel for the accused Mr. Naletilic. And I am going to ask you some questions about your previous testimony, and about the previous statements which you have given to various authorities. I will attempt to ask these questions in a manner which will allow you to answer with a short, short answer, and if the Prosecutor desires to follow up on any of your answers, he will have the right to do that during the redirect examination. Do you understand, Witness AA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you do understand that I will ask you some questions about your previous testimony, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And I would like for you to tell me if you do not understand my question. Will you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Again, will you tell me if you do not understand one of my questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. And I will not be trying to confuse you, so if you don't know the answer to a question, will you please just tell me you don't know the answer? Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. You just finished testifying about a very traumatic event, the loss of your mother; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, the witness gave his testimony in private session. Now we are in the open session. If you want to ask some questions which might identify the identity of this witness, we had better go back to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, may it please the Court. I would first apologise if I have asked any question that would identify this witness so far. I think I just asked him about his mother. I gave no names. But if it pleases Your Honour, I would ask then to go into private session for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness, were you aware that there were many displaced persons who had settled into Mostar in the Vranica building during the aggression with the Serbs in 1991, early 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And are you aware of who helped these displaced persons when they moved to Mostar and had been displaced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness, are you aware that there was an agreement between the ABiH commander Pasalic and the HVO commander Lasic that the headquarters for the 4th Corps would move from the Vranica building to another location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You testified that you had been a member of the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And what date was it that you stopped being a -- with the HVO and moved to the ABiH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the 19th of April, the sniper war had started, and I moved over some five or six days before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And can you tell me what period of time had you been with the HVO prior to the week before the 19th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometime from July 1992, July I think. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: There had not been any outbreak of aggression before you went over to the ABiH; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends on what you call the aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: The aggression between the Croats and the Muslims in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not physically, but there were other -- it took other forms, and there was also some physical manifestations but not too often.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So can you tell me, then, why it was that you went over to the ABiH from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I moved over from the HVO into the BiH army simply because I realised that there would be a war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness, that Pasalic had ordered the ABiH 4th Corps to join the HVO in order to gain information, guns and ammunition, and then return back to the ABiH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's not what you did, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't do what?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You didn't join the HVO in order to gain information, guns, ammunition, and then return to the ABiH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I already said in the beginning that I was just a foot soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you aware, Witness AA, that Alija Izetbegovic agreed that all headquarters in Mostar would be under the HVO control for the defence of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could I have the help from the usher for P14.2 for the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Meek. Is this a new exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No. Actually, it's P14.2. I'm sorry. P14.2. It's a map. It was shown yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, do you recognise this Exhibit 14.2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know what a map is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you see that this is a map of Mostar, or part thereof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you are very familiar with Mostar; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, so-so. I know the streets. I can find my way in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And on this Exhibit 14.2, can you find the location of the Vranica building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vranica building. It should be -- the Vranica building should be here, at the end of Stjepana Radica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could you point it out with the pointer, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Stjepana Radica, so if this is the end of the street, if that is the cross-section that I think it is, then the Vranica building should be here, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Will you take a pen, please, and mark where that building is located first. But also, can you diagram the outline of that building, since you know it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't draw, and I don't know what to tell you right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness, is it a rectangular building, is it an L-shaped building, is it a square building? The shape of the building is what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was L-shaped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Very well. Then would you please, to the best of your knowledge and recollection, draw that L-shaped building as it faces whichever streets it faces that you just pointed out with the pointer, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, thank you. Are you familiar with a street named Ante Zujanica Street in Mostar. It's spelled A-n-t-e --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ante Zujanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes. Are you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ante Zujanica. I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Put a mark where that street is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, while you're there, would you go ahead and mark a "1" where the building, the Vranica building was that you already located, and then go ahead and mark a number "2" by the street you just marked.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. You've testified that, I believe it was on the 10th of May, the shelling began in Mostar. Is that the correct date, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say the 10th. I said the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were able, with a group of other soldiers, to remain in this -- in or around this building until approximately the evening of the 10th of May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, was the shelling and firing on this building coming from all directions or mainly one or two directions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the shells fired on that building and the left bank were fired from the HVO front lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So would you draw the arrow towards which direction the shelling was coming from on this exhibit, please, with your pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bijeli Brijeg. From Bijeli Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Usher, could we turn that map?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So the artillery and the firing was coming from the direction at the top of this map now towards the middle of the L-shape and the back of the building; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you for right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, you indicated that the shelling had started in the morning, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: But you did not make it to the roof until sometime about 2.00 in the afternoon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Where were you for that six or eight hours prior to reaching the roof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the building and because of the logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And were you with the group of 15 to 20 soldiers that you testified about during that first six or eight hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I already said I had six soldiers with me. We were on the terrace at 8.00, before we climbed down to the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And approximately how many hours were you on the roof before you had turned yourself in the next day, the 10th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was on the roof between 2.00 in the afternoon until 8.00 or half past 8.00 in the evening, that I went out to the command at 9.00, and that we all turned ourselves in, that we all surrendered on the 10th sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You also testified that before you turned yourself in, you changed into civilian clothes, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you keep the civilian clothes with you that day? Had you had them with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So did you get back to your flat to get your civilian clothes to change into?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nope. I just entered the first flat and took some civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you know whose flat you stole these clothes from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I didn't steal those clothes. I took them. Don't insult me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm not trying to insult you, my friend. I just wondered whether you had any permission to take these clothes from the lawful owner.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can you prove the contrary?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm asking you: Did you have permission from the owner to enter the flats and take the clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I'm asking you: How are you going to prove that I didn't have Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the permission, even if I say I did? How will you know that I did have it indeed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Because I presume you're going to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look at this. It's a silly question. I apologise, but that's how it is, and who -- who would really ask questions about this civilian clothes? I'd really ask for a break so we can have a smoke together. I do apologise, Your Honours, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And will you tell me: What was the purpose to change into civilian clothes out of your military uniform before you left that building that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not leave the building. We surrendered. I changed into civilian clothes because I hoped I'd fare better.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's 11.00 and I'm about ready to quit this line of questioning. I think it might be a good time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Before you resume, could I ask you how long you are going to take for your cross-examination, for the sake of the arrangement of the sittings of today?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: It should be finished, Your Honour, by 45 minutes, depending on the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Seric or Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think we will need from 20 minutes to half an hour perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Scott, for the re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. -- that will depend, of course, on Mr. Bos. I wouldn't expect it to be extensive. I just thought I would share with the Chamber that if, in fact -- we had hoped to call one other witness this week, but my thinking would be if we get close to 15 or 20 minutes out from 1.00, I'm probably going to suggest to the Chamber that we just not start with that witness. He's only here locally, so it's not a huge scheduling issue. So it just depends on how much time we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Your Honours, for the record, the exhibit which was formerly P14.2, Madam Registrar has indicated to me is now D1/20, after Witness AA has made the marks he did this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean, "under the control."

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, who was your commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branko Kvesic was, while I was in the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And what was Branko's position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a minister in the government of the -- the so-called government of Herceg-Bosna, the minister for police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: The police. And so you worked underneath the minister of police as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: SIS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Then when you left this HVO minister of police duty, did you maintain and keep the weapons that had been given to you and your uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You turned those back in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you went to the ABiH and were in the 4th Corps logistics headquarters; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Then please explain what your duties were in the ABiH once you left the HVO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 19th of April, 1993, the so-called sniper war began in Mostar, and it lasted about ten days. After that, under an agreement between the politicians and the army leadership - I'm not sure exactly who - an agreement was reached for us to move into the police and to perform a joint service in Mostar. And then from Mostar, they asked us to move to the left bank of the river, so to move to the left bank of Mostar. So we didn't agree to that, and then we were transferred by UN vehicles to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not permitted to wear uniforms because this agreement had been reached only that the military police was allowed to carry weapons and pistols. After that, we moved from Cernica and our command was below Bulevar, and that's when we established the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, the interpreter did not get the name. You testified that we were transferred by UN vehicles to -- some location, I think. What location was that? The interpreter did not pick it up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Cernica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: To your knowledge, and in your knowledge, do you know how many commanders there were in the 4th Corps logistic headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know because I wasn't at the logistics headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. And you mentioned the political agreement just now regarding Mostar. My question would be, if you know, was that the Vance-Owen Plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that wasn't the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that you were then in the military police for the ABiH. What were your duties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We controlled the town at night. And we were also holding the lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: On the 9th -- between the 9th of May, when the shelling began in Mostar, and the time that you left the building, how many rounds do you believe that you fired that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you have an idea of how many weapons you had with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We only had a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Would I be right in assuming that all of the soldiers in that building who left with you were also armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you turn the guns and firearms over to the HVO when you left the building? Or what did you do with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We hid them in the entrance hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You have not mentioned in your direct testimony that anybody was killed in that action; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two were wounded from our soldiers and one member of the HVO was killed, and that was -- he was killed by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I understand, from your testimony and your statements that you have previously given, that you met and spoke with Mr. Naletilic, my client, as you first walked into the Tobacco Institute; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not talk to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You met with him, then, when you first entered the Tobacco Institute?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Brana Kvesic -- after Brana Kvesic called him, then we met.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And that was upon your initial arrival at the Tobacco Institute?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's where their main command was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could I have help with looking at the Exhibit P17 once again, the video that was shown yesterday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes. If we are going to show the video, I think we will at least need to go into private session and maybe into closed session. I'm not sure. There are many people in the public gallery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's just fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, about how far back had you seen my client, Tuta, before this day at the Tobacco Institute?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could be sometime in 1992, but I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you see him more than one time or just once?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I saw him only once, on that occasion, before this other instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you speak with him on that first occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you gave a description of Tuta as being approximately -- looking 70 years old; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't say that he was 70 years old. I said he looked old for his age, as if he were 70.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's correct, yes. Thank you. And yesterday, in your direct testimony, you indicated that you did not know my client's surname. That's a fact, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said I knew that he was Naletilic, that I didn't know his first name. I still don't know. All I know is that your client is Naletilic, and I know Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You testified that -- and by the way we just watched that video. There was an individual in that video with a Motorola in their hand, was there not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the soldiers perhaps. Perhaps one of them did have a Motorola. I didn't pay any attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. But to describe a Motorola that you discussed, it's not like a small cell phone that we have today, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. That's an army Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: An army Motorola is a large object, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, depends. At that time -- I wouldn't know, really, how big it was. Well, medium-sized, say. Neither too big nor too small. Like this. I'm saying like this, neither too big nor too small.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And for the record, the witness indicated approximately eight to ten inches. I'm sorry, I don't know centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, how thick was that Motorola?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: How thick? It depends on the type of battery that's used. There are batteries which will work for only two hours, and there are others which are long-lived which are slightly bigger, and it depends on that, really. I don't really know. Never measured it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Witness AA, I'm more interested in the specific Motorola that you allege Tuta had in his hand that day and struck you with.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. How big, if you know, was the Motorola that Tuta allegedly held in his hand and hit you with at the Tobacco Institute?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we could put it this way: It was so big that when you took it in your hand, there was still one part protruded under your palm, or rather fist, as you held it and the upper part also protruded upwards so that you could hit with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And which part did he allegedly hit you with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corner. As he held it like this, he struck that blow with the corner, with the very end of the Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And that would be the bottom end of the Motorola?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. And you testified yesterday that Tuta held the Motorola in his left hand and he hit you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he held the Motorola in his left hand? He could hold the Motorola in his right hand only because he was using his left hand to slap me in the face. As he stood in front of me, he used his right hand to strike these blows on my head. You just reversed the two things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So if your testimony on the record yesterday was that the Motorola was in my client's left hand, you were just simply mistaken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know what the transcript of yesterday says. I'm telling you, if I told you yesterday that he was slapping me on my left temple, then he couldn't hold -- on my right temple, then he couldn't hold the Motorola in his left hand because he was using it for that other thing. I don't know what was written down yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And today, on this answer, are you saying he hit you on your right temple today or your left temple?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said left temple.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And you said he struck approximately eight to ten blows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And didn't you tell the investigator that he hit you "full out"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. He wasn't caressing me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: When he hit you, did he hit you hard like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you expect me to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I just -- Witness AA, I'm not trying to confuse you; I'm just trying to understand with what degree of force these blows were allegedly given to you by my client. And if you would like to demonstrate on the desk, please feel free to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you have a Motorola in your right hand and then takes a swing and -- how do I know what force? I can't answer. It hurt, I can tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You never fell down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They never managed to fell me down while I was in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, no. My question was: When my client allegedly struck you these eight or ten times "full out" with this Motorola, at the Tobacco Institute, you stayed on your feet; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I've just told you that I'm an athlete and I managed to remain on my feet because I was strong, not because his blows were weak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You did not pass out, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that those were specific conditions, and one -- that is a struggle for life. I mean, you realise that you have to fight for your life and then you summon the strength which you need to survive. And you can't remember these things all that well. Because I simply couldn't allow them to knock me off my feet and humiliate me in that manner, and I summoned all my strength so as to stand -- to remain on my feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So you will admit that during these specific conditions, it is hard to remember things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not hard to remember things, but one will put up with more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you have no -- you didn't bleed that day and you don't have any scars on your left temple, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I said that I had a slight laceration, slightly. My skin was slightly rough. I don't know how to describe it. But otherwise, no, you can't see it, physically, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So you would agree with me that you were not seriously injured that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, I wasn't seriously injured? Isn't it a serious injury for you when they beat you, when you're beaten by five men as if you were a gypsy?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, I'm not -- we're not talking about being beaten by five men. Now we're talking about this alleged incident with my client hitting you on your left temple eight to ten times with the Motorola. That's my question. You did not receive any serious injury from that. There's no scar, you didn't pass out, you didn't even fall down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer this question. If I didn't fall down, if I didn't pass out, it does not mean that he did not beat me. Will you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. please try to understand that he simply could not knock me off my feet then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And these alleged blows to your left temple by my client have not caused any damage to your memory, have they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: My memory? Well, they didn't, now that I'm sitting here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in your testimony yesterday, you described and spoke about a soldier by the name of Juka. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And Juka was present at the Tobacco Institute on the day that you were allegedly struck by Tuta; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And in the presence of my client, Juka stopped the killing of some individuals, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And on that day, in the presence of my client, Juka stopped actually the beating of you, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. Not in the presence of your client. He was there, and he wasn't the only one present; there were other men there. That presence, when you talk about this presence, I don't really know how to explain it to you. He was not present -- he was not the only one with Juka there. There were others, too. So he was not present next to Juka when Juka said that they should stop beating me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, maybe we're -- I understand there were a lot of people there and that my client and Juka were not the only two people there, da? But my client was present when Juka stopped the killing, and also, Juka ordered Tuta to stop hitting the man name Pobric, did he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't order him. He said, "Don't beat him any more, because he is coming with me."

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And Pobric went with Juka and the hitting stopped; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You've already answered this, I think, but there were other military and civilian officers and people present at the Tobacco Institute, many; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you testify yesterday that you observed my client, Tuta, hit Pobric with the butt of a gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the butt of a gun but with a Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: This is Pobric, not you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. After he had finished beating me, he moved over to Pobric. These are two different cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And didn't you tell investigator Jan van Hecke back in 1997 that you really could not see what happened, that you heard it only?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, you were at some point taken to Siroki Brijeg; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you remained there for approximately two weeks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And were you allowed approximately three hours daily of outside air, to be outside in the air?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not outside air. In a classroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You were -- you were given good food there, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We did not get the witness's answer, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the interpreter did not get your answer, Witness AA. The interpreter did not get the answer to the last question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it depends.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, if you told investigator Jan van Hecke that the food was good there, you weren't lying to him, were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And while at the jail in Siroki Brijeg, you were given two meals a day, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Morning and evening, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could I have the usher, please, hand the witness a -- for the record, I do not intend to introduce this into evidence, but this is a statement given by this witness April 27, 1997, to investigator Jan van Hecke, and I would ask the usher to show him that page, the bottom paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could I ask my learned colleague which paragraph he's reading?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: It's the last paragraph. In Croatian language, it's the last paragraph, and on the English, for my colleague Mr. Bos, look on page 4 of the Jan van Hecke statement. It would be the third paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could someone read this paragraph, either in Croatian or in English, so that we could have the benefit of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'll be happy to, Your Honour. The paragraph starts: "Around the same time that I was beaten up by the five soldiers, it can't have been during one of the breaks in the beating but certainly after Tuta had beaten me, another prisoner in the row was beaten by Tuta. His name is Alica Pobric. I was standing the first from the right in the row, and Pobric was somewhere in the middle. I could not precise see what happened. I saw it from an angle of my eye. Tuta said something to Pobric that I could not understand, and I heard the hit. Immediately after the hit, Juka told Tuta not to beat Pobric again." The second sentence, the last sentence in that paragraph says, "I suppose Tuta -- that Tuta hit him with his Motorola." For the record, Juka is J-u-k-a.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, is that what you said in your statement to Jan van Hecke, the OTP Prosecutor investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I interject, Mr. Meek? My notion of what you said to this witness sometime back is that he had said to Mr. van Hecke that he had not seen Mr. Pobric being hit. That's quite different from what you have read out and indeed from what the witness said. The witness said that he could see what was happening from an angle. That's quite different from what you put to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Judge Clark, I'll ask another question, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think you should be more fair in your questions because that was a very specific question you put, that he said to Mr. Van Hecke that he did not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: It's a fair statement, Witness AA, that with Mr. Van Hecke, you told him that you really heard the hit and you supposed that it was with a Motorola, even though you had been looking from an angle of your eye. Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Let me explain this. The investigator asked me if I -- if it happened in front of my eyes directly, and I said that we were in a line, but that line wasn't all that straight, so it's not that I couldn't see it altogether. I was to the right. He was to my left. So I could see Tuta come up to him and somebody was hit and I saw him take a swing with his arm. What you are trying to say, "Did you see what he hit him with?" And I said I saw the Motorola in his hand. What this statement says, "perhaps hit him," it's not "perhaps." He hit him, except that it could have been a Motorola or it could have been a pistol. Now, we can discuss whether it was a Motorola or a gun, but I am saying that I saw a Motorola in his hand. Why I said "perhaps" is because I wasn't sure whether it was a Motorola, since we were in this line. I wasn't directly facing this, so that "perhaps" could apply to the Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness AA, and I think that you just said that you couldn't directly see, but yesterday you testified that you did see. I'll go on to something else.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can do this too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You gave a statement in Mostar about your time in Siroki Brijeg. Do you recall that statement January 8, 1996?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who did I give the statement to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You gave the statement to the Ministry of the Interior Security Services Centre, Criminal Police Sector, Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: In that statement, you spoke of Siroki Brijeg and going to work at a swimming pool, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And in that statement, you never mentioned that the swimming pool at Siroki Brijeg was Tuta's swimming pool, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: But when investigator van Hecke took your statement, you said it was Tuta's swimming pool, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. That's not correct. I didn't say it was Tuta's pool, but when they took us to work there, they said, "You're going to work on Tuta's pool." Up until that time, I didn't know that, because the home guards who drove us there told us we were going to be working on Tuta's pool, but before that I didn't know that it was Tuta's pool. Perhaps it isn't. How should I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And that pool was located in the centre of town, basically, was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May I have P26.10 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, this is a photograph that you looked at yesterday. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could you please take the pointer and point for the Trial Chamber where you were sitting on the day that some man came and kicked you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Let the record reflect that he pointed to the upper left-hand corner, which would be the shallow end of that swimming pool.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it wasn't there. It was in the middle of the pool.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, Witness AA, did you misunderstand my prior question? It was very simple. I asked where you were sitting when you were kicked, and you pointed to the upper left side of the swimming pool. Would you please then tell me where it was you were sitting, sir, when you were kicked.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not my fault that the pointer is so thick and I can't point it out precisely. If I had a more precise one, I would point it out. So I was in the middle part of the pool and not on the corner, but you can't see it because of this tree. That's what I showed earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness, I apologise, then. We would be looking at this exhibit, 26.10, and there's a swimming pool there, and on the left, in the picture, there are some trees, the tops of which obstruct the view to the -- that end of the swimming pool; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And in your last answer, that is where you were sitting, behind where those trees would be, and we could see that if the tops of those trees were cut down; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was sitting precisely in the middle of the pool.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, did you know this man who just walked up to you and did this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in my statement that he was the driver of the Minister for Provisions and Social Services and Welfare.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: But my question to you is: Was there some bad blood between you? Had you done something to this man or was this just a surprise that it happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't do anything to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You testified that at one point, my client came across the walkway and people were cheering. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And how many people were there that were cheering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. As many as there were guards there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And the guards were all military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were the Home Guards units. It was the older people who were on guard duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: The older people that would not have to go to the front to see action; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You didn't see my client that day stop and give any orders to anybody, though, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would he be giving orders? Because it had nothing to do with the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have knowledge of when the Convicts' Battalion was formed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that the Convicts' Battalion was formed at a time when the Serbs were the aggressors in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was. That's how it seems to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: One quick question on this swimming pool, then. You've already pointed out the shallow end of the pool where you were sitting. How many metres did you then fall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I gave my statement, at that time I said it was about five metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And are you sticking by that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim -- because I wasn't able to state it precisely, so I said five metres, but it means that it could have been between three and five metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Or perhaps less than one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It seemed as if it was 1.000 metres to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, in the time that the Serbs were the aggressors in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Convicts' Battalion had gained some sort of notoriety - would that be a fair statement - at least around the Mostar area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was -- it had that reputation in Mostar, but in Listica, it certainly did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you've indicated that there were soldiers that would take these patches, Convicts' Battalion patches, and sew them on a shirt and then maybe remove them and put them on another jacket from time to time when they went to Mostar; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I said that or not, but they did wear markings, but I don't know if they wore them when they went to Mostar. Perhaps I said that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... recollection that that was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, I don't think that was said in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you ever observe soldiers put on this patch on a particular shirt before they would go to a front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry. May I interrupt? It's quite important that the transcript should get that right. When I interjected, I said, "I have no recollection that that was said," and the opposite appears on the transcript. Just that if we're reading it in six months' time, it may be important.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Judge Clark, is it fixed now for your -- is it okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'm sure they will do it this evening, but what I have just said is recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: When you gave the statement to investigator Jan van Hecke, did you give it on only two days, or did you give it between April 27th and May 4th of 1997 and each day between those two dates, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you give it on only two days or one day? What?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And didn't you tell investigator Jan van Hecke that while you were in Siroki Brijeg, that the guards had HVO insignia on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't have said that, because I was at the police, downstairs, so they could only have had the police markings. So I don't know which guards you were asking about. If they were the guards at the pool, they had HVO markings, but at the prison where I was in Listica, it was the military or the civilian police, and they had the blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, while we're on that subject, the commander of the Heliodrom prison was Jusuf Praliak, P-r-a-l-i-a-k; is that correct? Was the answer yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I didn't see it on the screen. Who was the commander at Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the camp at Dretelj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And in each of these camps, the guards were military policemen, correct, with the white belts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't wear white belts but they were part of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, you told --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, could you please switch my monitor off? It's bothering my eyes. It's still turned on. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall giving a statement to the OTP investigator wherein you told him that you believed that the Convicts' Battalion was a kind of a myth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And can you please explain to the Trial Chamber why you believe that the Convicts' Battalion was a myth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a myth in that sense, but simply because they had more weaponry, they had more options to gain or to have weapons, artillery, infantry and other kinds of weapons. They drove jeeps. They had other vehicles. They had money. They could do whatever they wanted. That was the sort of thing that I meant by "myth."

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And when you state that it was something of a myth, it was because at least people believed that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're trying to say was a myth, that were simply -- that's how the others in the town of Mostar talked about them. They boasted about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Right. You would agree with me, Witness AA, that in wartime, rumours are floating around everywhere about all kinds of things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, what I mean is that people will say some things that, whether they are true or not, they get spread around to the general public, become rumours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends. You're asking me to respond to a question which is not specific. Tell me what you mean specifically. Do you want me to stay -- to say that there were more lies and false stories being told about the Convicts' Battalion than true ones? Is that what you're trying to get?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, Witness AA, I'm going to have to have the usher have you look at your statement again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And for Mr. Bos, it's page 6 of the Jan van Hecke statement, first full paragraph on page 6 in the English version. And Your Honours, I would just ask the witness to read that paragraph first before I ask him a question so we don't have to read everything.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read this to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No, no. I want you to just read it to yourself. Now, I asked you earlier, while you were in Siroki Brijeg, did you know about soldiers who would sew on the badges of the Convicts' Battalion before they would go to Mostar, to the front lines. Do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that they placed badges, these badges, of the Convicts' Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So they were not permanent? They could be taken off and placed on other items of clothing, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And please describe for the Trial Chamber what one of these Convicts' Battalion badges looked like. Please describe it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't one of the badges. There was only one. And that's the one that I know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Just please describe it for the record.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The badge was round and in two parts.
