In the top and in the bottom part, in a semi-circle, it said "Convicts' Battalion, Siroki Brijeg," and in the middle, there was something black in the shape of a snake, and then there was some -- a line or something at the bottom that kind of crossed over. I can't be quite precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Besides that something black in the shape of a snake, what other colour was this badge, this round badge you've just described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly now, but I think that all of the badges were brown-green. I can't remember the exact colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. We looked at a picture P26.7 yesterday, which was a cell in Siroki Brijeg at the jail. Do you recall that picture, Witness AA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: About -- was that room -- did you describe how many metres you thought that room was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already described it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And is it fair that you did say there were 20 people in that little room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, about 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you couldn't even sit down, could you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And then you described two additional people coming in that room, making approximately 22 people, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, you said that two guards made their way into the room.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. In all camps, when the guard comes in, we all have to step back to the corners, into the corners of the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I believe that from your description of the room, everybody was standing like sardines in a can; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Then you were taken to Ljubuski, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And there was only one guard on that bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, one or two. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you testified that when you arrived at Ljubuski, they took your cigarettes away from you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I don't recall that that was testified here in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Then let me ask it this way, then: When you arrived at Ljubuski, Witness AA, were your cigarettes taken away from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took away -- they confiscated everything that I had with me, all my things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Including your cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And my wallet and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So my question to you would be that who gave you the cigarettes in Siroki Brijeg? How did you get them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've stated that. I said that in my statement. They were given to me by a man whose name was Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: After you were released from the Heliodrom, you went back and you were a soldier with the ABiH army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I returned where? When I was released from the camp?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And your job was that you were the personal bodyguard for an individual, were you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And who was that individual?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I did not understand that. Do you have his full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is not important, I'd rather not talk about it. It has nothing to do with this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tend to agree with the witness, and if Defence insists, at least we should do it in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to go to private session very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we will go to private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, but apparently, and I'm looking at -- the transcript is not complete with that name, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is that name so important? I think that the typist will check this name at night. It will be corrected to reflect it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness AA, do you know the family name of this individual you've testified to who is called Cikota?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was his last name? Why, Cikota. I guess that is his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know -- are you aware that he was a policeman in Split?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Are you aware that he was a policeman in Split, Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And are you aware that he lived in Listica?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's all the questions I have of this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Par. With the cooperation from the interpreters and the court reporter, we could sit here a little bit longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness AA. I am a lawyer, Zelimir Par, and I'm one of the counsel for Vinko Martinovic, Stela. In your testimony, you mentioned a soldier called Romeo Blazevic, and you said that on one occasion he beat you, and that from a certain Rudi, the pilot, heard that he had also been beaten by the same Romeo Blazevic. Now, about this Romeo Blazevic, you said that he was Stela's soldier, or rather, you said something like that the whole of Mostar knew that Stela was his commander. Do you remember that part of your testimony? You do? Now, I have before me a document which was given me by the Prosecution with a list of names of soldiers, their units, and commanders, so I want to ask you to go through those lists together and then I will ask you some questions having to do with these lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Prosecutor's Exhibit P704, without the file number, from binder number 13, so could the witness please be shown this list and can we have it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Sir, Witness AA, let's have a look at this document. Tell me, on this first page that you see, what does it say above in the heading? Do you see this defence department, which is -- well, it says here Croat Defence Council, defence department, Convicts' Battalion, and beneath that, the Combat Group 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Will you now turn to page 2, and let's see the Combat Group 2. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Let's move on to page 3. Very well. Combat Group 3. Can you see that? You do. Good. And if we can then stop on the next page, which says the Combat Group 4. Can we see that page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, under 15, could you read out the name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Romeo Blazevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I see. Romeo Blazevic. Very well. And on the same page, under 1, could you please read out the name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it says Damjan Peric.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Damjan Peric. And next to him, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And his rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Captain. Very well. Now, you saw these documents, and could we agree that from this document that I've just shown you, it transpires that Romeo Blazevic was a member of the 4th Combat Group of the Convicts' Battalion and that his commander was Captain Damjan Peric? Can we agree that that is what transpires from that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's what I mean. Now, my question is: After you saw this document, are you still claiming that Vinko Martinovic, Stela, was Romeo Blazevic's commander, or would you allow that it was possible that his commander was this Damjan Peric, as this document says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But what you have just read out to me is the defence department of the Convicts' Battalion, and we have four combat groups here. Do you -- and I can tell you that Tuta was the -- above -- the top man here and that Stela was somewhere else, and maybe Stela also had his commanders under him, I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I'm asking you -- we can go back to this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I'm asking you: According to this document, does it transpire from it that Damjan Peric was Romeo Blazevic's commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And how can I know that this document is authentic? Well, anyone could print this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will please the witness and counsel not speak over one another.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, anyone could have -- could we please have a break? Could we have a small break?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could the counsel and witness please not speak simultaneously.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness has asked for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: But if I understand you well, you disregard this document and you stand by what you said yesterday about who was Romeo Blazevic's commander.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that he was his commander. I said that he was a member of the group which was called Stela's. I did not say that he was his commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I was informed that the witness is asking for a break. Is that true, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I think the witness is a rather heavy smoker and I think he needs a cigarette, so I wonder if we can just have a small break for a cigarette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we'll resume at 1.30, half past one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: That's fine with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, this Trial Chamber is informed that the witness is not feeling well so we cannot continue the cross-examination today. We will resume our hearings at 9.30 Monday morning. Is there anything to say -- yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, but I have a question, and I'm not asking for an immediate answer. All prisoners, and my client, can have family visits but they must be announced several weeks earlier, and my client's family would like to see him. I'd like to ask the Chamber if possible, not today but next week or sometime, could we be told whether we shall have some break in this case so that I could then reserve the time and the rooms for the visit of my client's family? Do we know if we shall have some days perhaps off during the case? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, just so there is no mystery about it, we had indicated after this witness, there was a Mr. Perlec would be testifying, but I think in light of this situation, which I'm not complaining but just for informational purposes, we won't call him in the next order. We will skip him. As soon as this witness is done, we want to take the next scheduled witness who is on the list. I won't mention his name but he's on the list. But we will just skip over Mr. Perlec, who Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. is here in The Hague, and then we will have to work him back into the schedule when we can. But just so there is no misunderstanding with counsel or the Chamber, we won't take him next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Well, as for the schedule of this trial, as well as the visits for your client, Mr. Seric, I think this Trial Chamber will consult with the Registrar concerning the matter. We hope we could give you an answer as soon as possible. So we will adjourn until 9.30 on Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
